correctness.rationale: With known nonzero magnitudes, equality of each nonzero bispectral triple is exactly u_j u_k=u_(j+k mod n), and zero triples impose no constraints. Positive (1,k−1) relations force u_k=t^k, negative (−1,−j+1) force u_−j=v^j, bridge (2,−1)→1 yields v=t^(−1); all phases are one signed ramp. For a nonwrapping permitted triple j+k−ℓ=0, this works for arbitrary t. Since supported signed frequencies lie [-s,r], largest potential positive wrap is 2r+s and largest negative wrap magnitude is 2s+r<2r+s; below n none is possible. At 2r+s≥n the explicit pair j=r, k=n−s−r lies in positive support and sums to −s mod n, imposing t^n=1. Cyclic shift acts by exactly these nth-root ramps since frequency 1 occurs. Constructed d−1 bridge/chain characters leave dimension one and an additional wrap character yields precisely n shifts; fewer characters cannot cut the real d-torus to identity component of rank one/finitely many points respectively. Independently enumerated all supported modular triples for (n,r,s)=(11,4,2),(11,5,1),(8,4,2),(13,5,3), obtaining no wrap only in first case. The rank proof, not a small Smith enumeration, supports all n.
